With two in the first positions, James and East well up in support, the team race was as good as won by the Bels. but a keen fight was going on for the second place between Highgate and Surrey W.C. with odds on the superior packing of Surrey to put them in front.

Three teams were entered from the club and again they continued to show progress, the highlight being the 3rd place of Syd James who walked exceptionally well and showed that he can satisfy the judges.
We actually started two full teams and a depleted third and our "A" Team of James, Hall, Checkley and Newson were 3rd to Highgate with 38 points.

His 100 metres in 10.4 was a tenth better than Ernie could manage in 2nd place, himself ahead of the local talent. A close 200 race gave Ernie a win over Trevor Hoyte (TVH/UK) and James (Australia) - all three timed at 21.3.

While all this was going on, Lionel still found time to marry his charming wife Pat, raise a family, (Robert, Katherine and James who have also turned out in Club Colours) and advance his career as a chef with the Royal Household.
Going out again Major seemed to be getting the better of Freary and Yusuf who were battling with SLH's James and Sykes with the leading Thames men also in close order.
James Ellington wanted a stiff test in the A 100 and got it. Only 4/100ths covered the first four and it was James just out of the ‘medal’ positions.
An “as expected” run came from James Fairbourn in the U20 men’s 10k – the sole survivor of a team that had threatened to medal before a variety of problems took out Messrs.
Highlights for Belgrave were the return to 400 hurdling of Ryan Dinham after injury - he won comfortably - and a masterly 3000m win from James Kelly.

Our third placed long relay squad were disqualified for a claimed faulty hand over (0 points) and then the triple jump results came in where javelin man James Everard backed up an injured Gary Wilson.
James Fairbourn had also been bothered by sickness over the last few days and each time he completed a circuit, resisted the temptation to come out.
Already the team race was clearly a Beagles v Bedford affair but with three Belgravians – James Fairbourn, Rich Stannard and Will Cockerell in the 80s, third place might just have been ours.

But our own James Kelly was up against Ben Moreau and try as he might, with a time 15th best on the day, James could not stop Moreau prising the gap open again to 45 seconds as the AFD man ran the day’s third best.

On match day this had fallen to just James Ellington as Darren Chin had pulled an abductor doing Friday evening start practice. But worse still was to come; James had a trapped sciatic nerve which reduced his stride length.

As has been the custom of recent years, the Bels competed strongly in the men’s race, pulling off a comfortable win – even though last leg man James Kelly went off course and ran for 20 seconds before deciding that he was in unfamiliar territory and had better return to the designated route.
